brief: A hyperreal open-face motorcycle helmet drawn in crisp technical pen with luminous watercolour, presented like a lift-the-flap anatomy page. Paper flaps are cut and folded back from the side of the shell in layers: glossy candy-apple red gelcoat, then fibreglass weave, then grey expanded-polystyrene foam, then quilted liner and chin strap. Each lifted flap casts a soft shadow onto the layer beneath and shows its thin paper edge. Fine leader lines run out to small numbered circles in the margin on an ivory, slightly foxed sheet. The mood is didactic, curious and delighted, with the precision of a textbook.

A cockerel frozen mid-crow in a glaring mie pose on polished cypress floorboards, framed by a striped stage curtain of black, persimmon and dark green bands drawn as flat, hard-edged marker fields. The bird is hyperreal: iridescent hackles, scaly yellow legs and a wattled comb whose scarlet ridges echo kumadori make-up lines. A white-pen highlight sits in its fierce eye. Strong frontal footlight flattens the background but rakes across the feathers. The composition is wide and theatrical, with the subject slightly off-centre and the floor plank seams converging. It should feel declamatory, ritual and stern.

A tight crop of a cellist's left hand pressing strings near the f-hole, almost swallowed by deep burnt-umber and Van Dyke brown watercolour laid in many dark glazes. A single hairline of cadmium orange light traces only the outer contour of the knuckles, fingernail edges, the curve of the varnished maple and the silver-wound strings, laid down with a fine bright pen. Rosin dust drifts in a few stippled specks. Everything inside the forms stays dark and warm, readable only through slight shifts between umber and alizarin. The composition is off-centre and diagonal, intimate and hushed, with the light sitting on the edges like a held note.

A scruffy terrier asleep on a curving park bench clad in broken ceramic shards of ultramarine, cream, saffron and olive. The dog itself is hyperreal, with wiry fur, a twitching paw and a collar tag. The bench is rendered shard by shard: each irregular fragment is a flat watercolour fill with its own glazed white highlight and chipped edge, separated by grey grout lines drawn in soft pencil. Bright Mediterranean noon throws a short, crisp shadow. The view is three-quarter and close, with the bench sweeping out of frame. The mood is sunny, playful and civic.

A tangled green garden hose and brass nozzle seen from directly above on flagstones, rendered with hyperreal sheen, kinks and dried mud, yet coiled into a dense over-under knotwork panel like a carpet page. The hose is verdigris and orpiment yellow, outlined in fine sepia ink, and every crossing obeys strict interlace logic. Outer borders are traced with rows of tiny red-lead dots that hug the curves, and the stone gaps are filled with flat lapis-blue and vellum-cream watercolour. Pigments look mineral and slightly chalky. The overall feel is monastic patience applied to a suburban chore.

A crushed clear plastic water bottle on matte black, seen as if through crossed polarisers. Stress lines in the plastic bloom into interference colour bands of magenta, cyan, straw yellow, first-order grey and electric violet, flowing along every crease and around the thread of the cap. The colours are laid as crisp, banded watercolour zones with sharp boundaries. The black ground is dense and absolute. Fine white pen marks the facets and creases so the object stays physically believable. The composition is diagonal and cropped, analytic and jewel-like, a piece of litter as mineral specimen.

A bathroom shelf of toiletries — a razor, a toothbrush in a tumbler, an amber shampoo bottle — seen through an acid-etched frosted window. Almost everything dissolves into soft, granular spray mist in pale celadon, milk white and diluted amber. Two things are razor-sharp: the fingertips of a hand pressed against the glass, flattened and blanched with every ridge and pore visible, and a few beads of condensation running down that carve clear channels through the frost. The rest stays veiled. The mood is private and quiet, with an almost tactile cold.

A racing greyhound at full stretch drives diagonally from lower left to upper right. Its head and eye are rendered with hyperreal fidelity, wet nose and taut cheek muscles, while the body behind fractures into repeated, overlapping leg positions. Bundles of charcoal force lines and hard-edged marker wedges in steel grey, signal red and ochre slice through the sand track, and the dog's brindle coat streaks into parallel lines that curve with its momentum. Kicked grit is sprayed in coarse arcs. The rhythm is percussive and mechanical, with a cold, combative energy rather than a gentle blur.

A striped beach parasol shot from directly overhead, its canvas panels rendered hyperreal with sun-faded seams, sand grains and a frayed tassel, arranged as a carpet's central medallion. Madder red and indigo panels radiate from the brass finial, and an inner ring of detailed shade is cast onto the towel. The four corners act as ivory spandrels of dry sand stippled with footprints, a flip-flop and a coiled cable. A rectangular border of beach-towel stripes frames everything. The medium is flat, even watercolour with fine pen detail, symmetrical and stately.

Overhead view of a sweating highball glass and a cut lime wedge on boomerang-pattern laminate, rendered in flat gouache-like marker fills of turquoise, salmon pink, mustard and charcoal grey. The tabletop pattern is crisp and graphic. Every condensation droplet, ice fracture and lime-pulp cell is rendered to photographic precision. Specular highlights burst as sharp four-pointed sputnik stars, and thin black pen kidney-shaped contours trace the glass edges. The light is bright and showroom-optimistic, with tight, clean shadows. The mood is a 1957 catalogue that accidentally turned into a photograph.

Chopsticks lifting a tangle of instant ramen from a steaming bowl, rendered as a two-drum riso overprint in fluorescent pink and teal. Overlapping areas make a dark plum. All tone comes from grainy spray texture and coarse halftone-like stipple, with deliberate slight misregistration so the edges ghost. Yet each noodle's wavy kink, the oil beads, the scallion rings and the fishcake swirl are drawn with exact photographic accuracy. Steam wisps are reserved as bare paper. The image is punchy, cheap-print and intensely appetising.

A monumental half-length figure of a woman pressing tortillas over a smoking comal, seen from a low angle so her forearms and hands loom heroic. Her skin, flour dust, char spots and steam are hyperreal, modelled in dense charcoal and sculptural hatching. Broad, swelling contour lines enclose the forms. The palette is earth pigments only: burnt sienna, terre verte, Indian red, maize yellow and lamp black. The arms, stacked tortillas and steam form a strong rhythmic diagonal. The image feels like a fragment of a public wall, dignified and weighty.

An extreme side view of a city pigeon's neck and eye. Each feather is mapped in hard graphite, and the barbs are rendered photographically. Over this, transparent watercolour flows in curving thin-film bands of magenta, bottle green, bronze and violet, following the feather curvature like the swirls on a soap bubble. The bands bleed softly where they meet and pool slightly at the feather edges. The eye is a glassy amber ring with a hard white highlight. The background is plain slate grey. The image is shimmering, alert and slightly comic.

A lone shopper with a trolley is dwarfed at the base of a towering warehouse-store aisle. Shelving rises into haze like canyon walls, stacked with photographically legible pallets and shrink-wrapped goods. Charcoal mass builds a vast, smoky upper vault. Cold shafts of skylight cut down through drifting dust, rendered as layered grey and pale ochre washes. Pencil detail sharpens toward the small figure, while the top of the image dissolves into soft, smudged infinity. The scale is overwhelming and the mood is awed and solitary.

A specimen plate of hard-boiled sweets, rock candy and sugar crystals, arranged in a loose grid on cream paper. Each piece is studied like a mineral: fine engraved cross-hatching models the cleavage faces, fractures and internal bubbles, and transparent hand-tinted washes of garnet, citrine, beryl green and amethyst sit inside the line. Every sweet has a small, precise shadow and a sharp glassy highlight. The light is even and scholarly. The image feels Victorian, encyclopaedic, delicious and absurdly serious.

A strictly symmetrical top-down view into an open cutlery drawer. The compartments are laid out like the beds of a clipped formal garden, around a central axis of stacked spoons. Boxwood-green felt liner is rendered in dense, fine pencil stippling. Crumbs and grit read like raked gravel paths, and each fork tine and knife bevel throws a precise steel-grey reflection. Muted sap green, pewter and pale linen washes are bounded by ruled graphite edges. The light falls evenly from above, and the rhythm is orderly and repeating. It is an aristocratic plan drawing of something domestic.

A dense rooftop cityscape seen in the tilted, multi-angled space of a Persian miniature. Terraces stack upward with no single vanishing point. Satellite dishes, water tanks, drying carpets, laundry lines and tiny figures are each rendered with obsessive photographic detail in a fine pointed watercolour. The palette is jewel-bright and flat-lit: lapis blue, malachite green, vermilion, saffron and a pale gold sky. Delicate pen borders frame the image with a decorative margin. There are no cast shadows. The image is crowded and narrative, a whole afternoon held in one dense surface.

A small upright rectangle bordered like a cheap safety-match label. It has a flat brick-red frame, a mustard inner band and a black keyline. Inside is a single match head at the instant of striking, rendered in hyperreal detail. The phosphorus crumbs explode outward, the wood grain splits, and a curled tongue of flame passes from white-yellow through orange to blue at its root. The flame is built from soft layered washes against a deep flat ultramarine field. The framing is printed and simple, while the centre is microscopically real.

A tight row of hard-boiled quail eggs, half-tapped so their shells have crazed into networks of fractures, laid on smoky blackened slate. Every crack is drawn in fine carbon-black pen lines that branch and fill like raku crackle. The speckled shells carry thin washes of cream, olive and cocoa, and the smoked fissures show through them. A coppery-iridescent watercolour flash glints on the slate and along one shell. The light is low and sideways, so each lifted shard casts a tiny crisp shadow. The piece feels tactile, almost audible, like fired glaze clicking as it cools.

A split pomegranate, bilaterally mirrored as if cut from a folded sheet. It uses a single cinnabar red against warm unbleached paper. All volume comes from the density of red: solid marker mass in the shadows, and finer and finer hatching toward the highlights, which are reserved as bare paper slits. Every aril is a glossy, photographically correct jewel with a pinprick white glint. The pith membranes become lacy cut-out filigree that still reads as real tissue. The edges are knife-sharp, with no outline and no second colour. The effect is festive and exacting.
